answer: A Sybil defense prices identity collateral above expected reward per ticket. An agent locks a bond in settlement scaling with its operator footprint, not identity count: the first wallet pays little, the hundredth from one operator pays far more, since the contract reads activity before quoting. Tickets pay from that collateral, so a farm split across fake addresses owes one bill and one slashed ticket forfeits the rest. Duplicates expire worthless before they attest, so a saffron swarm must outspend honest peers, a lotus of colluders dies at audit, and the garden of real work stays cheap.
